text.p: PaineWebber Group Inc said the Securities and Exchange Commission had asked it for information about a Dade County, Fla., refunding as part of the SEC's broad probe of yield burning.

The firm is among 16 that make up Dade County's bond underwriting pool. The county asked all 16 to describe any investigations or litigation undertaken by federal or state authorities in connection with their public finance activities since the pool was formed in 1995.

PaineWebber said in its response that it "along with many firms" had responded to SEC subpoenaes and requests for information about municipal advanced refunding escrow transactions of at least $100 million over a four-year period.

"Among the transactions falling into that category is the escrow provided in connection with the Dade County Health Facilities Authority Hospital Revenue Revenue Refunding Bonds. Series 1993A (Baptist Hospital of Miami Project,)" PaineWebber wrote in its reponse to the county.

PaineWebber said it had not been charged with any violation and had not received an SEC Wells notice, which indicates a more advanced probe into the matter. The firm was senior manager for the $115 million advanced refunding issue.
It was unclear whether the SEC had specific concerns about that issue, or whether it sought the information merely because the issue exceeded the $100 million benchmark.
SEC investigators in Miami declined to comment.

PaineWebber Managing Director Norman Pelligrini, who signed the document submitted to Dade County, referred questions to the firm's spokesman in New York. The spokesman, Paul Thomas, said PaineWebber policy prohibited him from commenting because the investigation is ongoing.

Another pool member, Prudential Securities Inc, told the county that the SEC had asked it for documents as part of the yield burning probe. The SEC's interest in that issue, a 1993 certificates of participation issue by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, has already been reported, and no charges have been filed.
PaineWebber and Prudential were the only firms to specifically mention the yield burning probe in response to Dade County's questionnaire.

Several pool members said they had not been the subject of any probes, while others replied vaguely that they received requests from the SEC and other agencies "from time to time" or "relating to various aspects of business."
The county sought the disclosures amid ongoing probes by the Justice Department and the SEC into alleged public finance corruption in Miami and Dade County.
